status_summary: Force Design continues under the Commandant's 2025 Force Design Update, released 2025-10-23. The Marine Corps force design page states that 3d Marine Littoral Regiment reached initial operating capability in December 2023, 12th Marine Littoral Regiment is projected to reach it in 2026, and 4th Marine Regiment is retained as a reinforced infantry regiment rather than converted into a third littoral regiment (Military Times reports the same). For the light amphibious ship, P.L. 119-21 provides 160 million dollars in advance procurement and about 1.8 billion dollars for Landing Ship Medium procurement per CRS, Sec. 127 of the FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60, 2025-12-18) authorizes contracts for not more than 15 Medium Landing Ships after a 30-day advance certification to Congress, CRS reports the Navy selected the LST-100 design in December 2025, and on 2026-07-13 the Navy announced a 2.2 billion dollar Vessel Construction Manager contract to TOTE Services LLC for initial production of up to eight Medium Landing Ships (one assigned to Bollinger Shipyards and four to Fincantieri Marinette Marine, with the approach for up to three more left to TOTE), with first delivery expected in fall 2029 and, per Defense News, construction to begin later in 2026. Federal law (10 U.S.C. 8062(b), added in 2022) already requires not less than 31 operational amphibious warfare ships, 10 of them assault ships; the 381-ship plan described by CRS includes 18 LSMs against a Marine Corps goal of 35. The update describes a rifle squad led by a school-trained sergeant, and no source was found on E-6 squad leaders, specific divestments or the current count of amphibious ships.

timeline.event: Reconciliation law P.L. 119-21 enacted; per CRS its Sec. 20002 provides 160 million dollars in advance procurement and about 1.8 billion dollars for Landing Ship Medium procurement.

Commandant issues the 2025 Force Design Update; the Marine Corps force design page states that 3d Marine Littoral Regiment reached initial operating capability in December 2023, that 12th Marine Littoral Regiment is projected to reach it in 2026, and that 4th Marine Regiment is retained as a reinforced infantry regiment, with two littoral regiments and one reinforced regiment described as the best composition for III MEF. The page also describes a return to a 13-Marine rifle squad with three fire teams led by a school-trained sergeant, a three-phase Medium Landing Ship program, and the statutory floor of 31 operational amphibious ships.

(month-only date) The Navy announced that it selected the Damen LST-100 design for the initial Medium Landing Ships, with construction expected from late 2026 and first delivery wanted by 2029, per CRS report R46374 (updated 2026-01-13).

FY2026 NDAA signed as P.L. 119-60. Sec. 127 authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to contract for not more than 15 Medium Landing Ships, including additions to existing contracts, after certifying to the congressional defense committees at least 30 days beforehand on force structure consistency, savings, funding, design stability and cost estimates. Per U.S. Code notes, the Act did not change the 31-ship floor in 10 U.S.C. 8062(b) but added a paragraph on prioritizing maintenance to keep the minimum number of amphibious warfare ships available.

The Navy announced a 2.2 billion dollar Vessel Construction Manager contract to TOTE Services LLC for the Medium Landing Ship program: TOTE holds the prime contract and is to manage shipbuilder subcontracts for initial production of up to eight ships, with one assigned to Bollinger Shipyards and four to Fincantieri Marinette Marine and the contracting approach for up to three more left to TOTE, and first delivery expected in fall 2029.

title: Marine Corps: continue Force Design 2030, light amphibious ships, 28 to 31 large amphibs
uncertainties: Force Design 2030 began before 2025 and this record covers actions since 2025-01-20 only, so the stage reflects continuation rather than new action on most items. The Force Design Update content was read from the Marine Corps force design web page, not the update document itself; the page is silent on divestments of tube artillery or law enforcement battalions, and gives no dates for the squad change or the Medium Landing Ship phases. Sea Power gives the release date as 2025-10-23 and the Marine Corps press release confirms it; Military Times says early October. Sec. 127 of P.L. 119-60 was read in the GovInfo text up to the sixth certification item, where the retrieved text ended. The earlier review wording that the statutory floor does not say operational is superseded: the U.S. Code text states 31 operational amphibious warfare ships. The statutory floor predates the review period. The count of amphibious ships and the amphibious content of the May 2026 shipbuilding plan were not retrieved. The LSM funding total adds CRS's two figures, and P.L. 119-21 itself could not be read because the GovInfo text is cut short. Independent review of 2026-10-16: a Military Times report of 2025-10-31 (a Maritime Reconnaissance Company, two littoral regiments kept, no third conversion) was moved here from the timeline as press coverage of the 2025-10-23 update; the LST-100 selection is dated to December 2025 (month only) per CRS, which cites reports of 2025-12-05 to 2025-12-09. Searches through 2026-11-02 for later Medium Landing Ship contract actions, and for an amphibious-fleet change in the Navy shipbuilding plan, found only the 2026-07-13 award; whether the up to three further ships in the Navy release are within or beyond the eight (Defense News treats them as the remainder of the eight) and whether they were awarded, and the amphibious content of any FY2027 shipbuilding plan, were not verified. The Defense News start-of-construction timing is a news report not repeated in the Navy release.
